Why does mean() return NA for my income column? 我已经检查过数据了。

In R, mean() returns NA as soon as one value in the vector is missing. R doesn't guess what the missing value was, so it reports the average as unknown too.

To average only the values you have, pass na.rm = TRUE:

mean(income, na.rm = TRUE)
x¯=1n∑i=1nxi

在删除缺失值之前，先检查两件事：缺失了多少，以及它们是否随机缺失。如果收入较低的受访者更常跳过这个问题，删除缺失值之后的平均值就会偏高。

Here n counts only the values that are present. Lecture 3 walks through both checks.
